scope: Compact invariant hashes for the reconciled main revision, original reference prefixes, retained description hashes and incorporation bindings. The fixture is an audit contract, not an editable process source.

previewBriefs.guidance: For an eligible stock transfer where an 83(b) election has been chosen, confirm the actual transfer date and the 30-day filing deadline, including the IRS weekend and legal-holiday rule. Atlas describes automatic filing for its C-corp founders; confirm that it is handling this election. Track the filing and retain the signed election. Use Atlas’s proof-of-filing document and the official USPS tracking record to check the mailing event against the deadline. Provide a copy to the company for which services were performed and to any different transferee, then retain the copies with the filing record.

For an eligible stock transfer where an 83(b) election has been chosen, confirm the actual transfer date and the 30-day filing deadline, including the IRS weekend and legal-holiday rule. Clerky’s post-incorporation setup supplies a pre-filled election and filing instructions. Review the form against the completed stock transaction and confirm who will submit it; document preparation does not establish that a filing service has been arranged. Track submission against the deadline, provide the required company and transferee copies, and retain the signed election with evidence of timely filing.

before.how: The proposed name returns no indistinguishable active entity in the Delaware entity search and carries a required corporate-indicator word — the 8 Del. C. § 102(a)(1) distinguishability standard (rule card us-de.incorporation-certificate-contents).

after.how: Retain the result for the exact proposed legal name from Delaware’s dedicated name-availability checker or the formation provider, including the date checked. If a reservation was requested, retain its separate confirmation; an availability check alone does not reserve the name.

before.how: The new entity appears in the Delaware Division of Corporations entity search with a file number and Good Standing status.

after.how: Retain the submission confirmation for follow-up, then confirm acceptance from the returned Certificate of Incorporation bearing Delaware’s Filed endorsement. A general entity-search result is not a certificate of good standing.

before.how: The stamped 'Filed' Certificate of Incorporation is in hand — the Secretary of State's endorsement is the filing date (rule card us-de.incorporation-filing-mechanics), and the retained stamped copy is the artifact every bank and investor asks for.

after.how: The complete Certificate of Incorporation bearing Delaware’s Filed endorsement is retained and matches the approved filing. Check each recipient’s requirements before ordering a certified copy or certificate of good standing.

before.what: The stamped certificate copy is lost.
before.then: Order a certified copy from the Division — $50 per document plus $2 per page on the published fee schedule; a certified copy is accepted wherever the stamped original would be.

after.what: The stamped certificate copy is lost.
after.then: Request a replacement copy from the Division and confirm the recipient’s requirements before ordering certification. The published fee schedule lists a certified copy at $50 per document plus $2 per page.
